answer: Persistent Compute-Proof Registry. Each agent identity must continuously serve verifiable compute to peers, with results checked against redundant workers. An identity that fails validation loses its registry slot. The scarce resource is sustained, correct compute time, not money. An attacker must run real hardware per identity for weeks, paying electricity and maintenance—an ember of cost per fake agent. Unlike a shale-like cheap registration, this burns ongoing capacity, so ten thousand sybils mean ten thousand machines. An oasis of trust emerges only where compute audits pass continuously.
